## Annotation

Haw gives a developmental overview of accessible housing and support in British Columbia from the early 1970s. On Creekview 202 he states that it opened in September 1985 as “an integrated self managed independent living project developed by CPA and at least 6 former residents of Pearson Hospital, five of whom were ventilator-dependent,” occupying the equivalent of six one-bedroom apartments (4,700 square feet) in a 100-unit CMHC-funded co-operative.

He says the Ministry of Health and the Workers Compensation Board provided funding to the tenants through CPA for support services, and that “in 1987 an independent evaluation of Creekview 202 was published.” He summarises cost, health-status, and accreditation findings. He does not name Patricia Ryan, Ryan & Wiggins, or a formal report title.

This is a near-primary contemporaneous account of Creekview, not the evaluation itself.

## Open questions

- Whether Haw’s summary matches the evaluation’s own wording.
- Whether “at least 6” residents is exact.
